title: Eyes and ears
hook: the impurity of the eyes is coveting, of the ears is gossip (Asa di Var, ang 472)

segments.voice: Yesterday, sootak, and your line: clean tongue. Did you catch an exaggeration and say the plain version? Yesterday's salok named the mind and the tongue. Today it goes on to the eyes and the ears. Day five hundred fifty-seven.

Scroll for ten minutes and count what comes in. Someone's new kitchen. Someone's vacation. A car you can't afford. A rumor about a person you've never met, and three hundred comments about it. None of it touched your hands. You didn't say a word. And yet the phone goes down with something new in it: a small want for what's theirs, a small taste for the rumor. Long before any feed, Guru Nanak named the two doors those come in through.
screen: `TEN MINUTES OF SCROLLING.` → `A SMALL WANT, A SMALL TASTE FOR RUMOR.` → `TWO DOORS IT CAME IN THROUGH.`

segments.voice: Here's the rest of the salok on ang 472, in paraphrase. The sootak of the eyes is looking with desire at another's spouse, another's wealth, another's beauty. The sootak of the ears is taking in slander, feeding on gossip. And then the last line: Nanak, even those who seem like swans, pure and bright, are bound and led away, if they carry these. Look at how exact this is. The eyes aren't impure for seeing. They're impure for a certain kind of looking: the look that wants what belongs to someone else. Coveting. It's quiet. Nobody else can see it. But it changes the one doing it, because every look that wants another's life makes your own life look smaller. The ears aren't impure for hearing, either. Gurbani is meant to be heard, sung aloud as kirtan. The impurity is in what the ears are fed. The salok's word for it is laaitbaaree: talebearing, backbiting, the tale carried about someone who isn't there. The salok pictures the ears almost eating it. And gossip, like coveting, doesn't need you to do anything. You just have to listen, and enjoy it a little. Put yesterday and today together and you have four doors: mind, tongue, eyes, ears. Greed, lies, coveting, gossip. Guru Nanak's point across all of it is the same. Washing the outside is easy. Keeping these four doors clean is the real purity, and it happens many times a day, in moments nobody else will ever see.
screen: `THE EYES: COVETING.` · `THE EARS: FEEDING ON GOSSIP.` · `IT CHANGES THE ONE WHO DOES IT.` · `FOUR DOORS: MIND, TONGUE, EYES, EARS.` · then, large: `CLEAN EYES, CLEAN EARS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look and listen cleanly. Sit and let your eyes rest on something simple in front of you: a wall, a cup, the sky. Just see it, without wanting it or judging it. Then close your eyes and listen to the sounds around you: traffic, a fan, a bird. Just hear them, without a story. Notice how quiet the mind gets when the eyes and ears simply receive. If you pray, you can let the word Waheguru be the one thing you listen to inside. The bell holds the time.
Laaitbaaree, talebearing or backbiting: in Guru Nanak's salok, the eyes' impurity is coveting what is another's; the ears' impurity, laaitbaaree, is feeding on gossip.
Your line: clean eyes, clean ears. Today, when a conversation turns to someone who isn't there, change the subject, or simply stop listening. Day five hundred fifty-seven.

howItsDone: Sikhs hear this salok of the four impurities in the dawn singing of Asa di Var, and Sikh teaching counts avoiding slander and coveting as part of daily discipline.

match.prompt: the four doors — tap the pairs.

myth: the salok says the eyes are impure for seeing anything at all
the impurity is a certain look: wanting another's spouse, wealth or beauty.
the salok's word for what the ears take in is slander, talebearing
laaitbaaree: the tale carried about someone who isn't there.
Gurbani is meant to be heard; the impurity is in what the ears are fed.

fork.setup: your friends start sharing a juicy rumor about someone who isn't in the room. what does the salok call this?
fork.reveal: the sootak of the ears is taking in slander. it doesn't need you to do anything; you only have to listen and enjoy it.

trapdoor: what you thought: don't look at bad things, don't listen to bad things.
what it means: the eyes are made impure by coveting another's life; the ears by feeding on gossip about someone absent.
what a scholar hears: 'akhee sootak vekhnaa par tria par dhan roop; kanee sootak kann pai laaitbaaree khaahi': the ears eat the tale.

sources.ref: Asa di Var, salok M1 (man kaa sootak lobh hai), Ang 472
